# Overview 

The Pacific Salmon Foundation's [State of Salmon Report](https://stateofsalmon.ca) aims to provide the public with answers to general questions regarding the state of salmon in British Columbia (BC) and the Yukon, such as:

* How are salmon populations doing? 
* What are the major factors influencing the state of salmon? 
* What is being done - and what could be done - to mitigate threats and recover salmon populations and the habitats they depend on?

This report, first released in September 2024, takes a data-driven approach to provide historical perspective and context for current news about salmon returns. The State of Salmon Report is being updated annually to reflect new data and changes to the state of Pacific salmon populations. 

As part of this work, PSF's [Salmon Watersheds Program](https://www.salmonwatersheds.ca) has developed simple metrics to report on the status and trends in regional abundance for each species. This document outlines the  specific data sources and analytical approach that we used to estimate time series of spawner abundance and total abundance (including catch) for each species and region, as well as draft results. Our analyses are ongoing, and the information here is subject to change on a regular basis, but we will endeavor to keep it up-to-date.

# Methods

## General Approach

We report spawner abundance for each of ten regions that represent all major Pacific salmon-bearing watersheds in Canada: Yukon, Northern Transboundary, Haida Gwaii, Nass, Skeena, Central Coast, Fraser, East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets, West Vancouver Island, and Columbia. These regions are also used to organize data in the [Pacific Salmon Explorer](https://www.salmonexplorer.ca). Note that there was a change from the 2024 Report to split the former Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets region into two to better reflect the unique ecology and environments of salmon between West Vancouver Island and East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets. There are a relatively small number of Pacific salmon that spawn in the MacKenzie River basin in Arctic Canada that are currently not included in the State of Salmon report.

We report on six species of Pacific salmon (*Oncorhynchus* spp.): Chinook, chum, coho, pink, sockeye, and steelhead. For each species, we report on state and trends based on generational averages. For pink salmon, we take the running average of even- and odd-year lineages, but do not separate assessments of even- and odd-year pink populations as is sometimes done in status assessments due to their consistent 2-year life cycle. Our approach of using generation running averages also smooths over dominant years for sockeye salmon, for which many populations display cyclic dominance. Shifts in dominance between even- and odd-year pink populations or declines in sub-dominant years of sockeye salmon are considered in a more nuanced way in our reporting when discussing how changes in abundance have been reflected in the diversity and distribution of each species within the region. 

For each of these species, where data are available, we construct an index of **spawner abundance** at the regional scale. We focus on spawner abundance because these data are more readily accessible and easily summarised at different spatial scales. Spawners represent the abundance of salmon available to reproduce and contribute to future generations, as well as to meet cultural and ecological needs within watersheds, and thus provides a measure of status relevant to communities and ecosystems. We recognize that commercial catch has historically been a substantial portion of salmon that return to the coast, and that ignoring declines in catch will underestimate the declines in overall salmon abundance. There is also increasing rates of pre-spawn mortality (i.e. mortality of salmon after their enter the river but before they successfully spawn) that mean that spawner abundance may be less than the number of fish that survive to maturity Therefore, where data are available, we include information on **total abundance** (i.e. the number of salmon that survive to maturity, calculated as spawners plus catch plus pre-spawn mortality (where applicable)). 

We have based our assessments on the best available data for each region and species. For example, stocks that are governed by international treaties may be monitored by the [Pacific Salmon Commission (PSC)](https://www.psc.org/), and tend to have reliable time series of abundance available at regional scales. These data sources are outlined in the [Region-Specific Data section](#region-specific-data). For species and regions where aggregate abundance is not reported by the PSC or DFO at the scale needed, we adapted our approach to make the best use of available data. In most cases, this meant expanding spawner abundance from stream-level estimates to get a regional scale index of spawner abundance using two types of expansion factors [@EnglishEtAl2018NorthCentralCoast]. This expansion process is described in the [Expansion Factors section](#expansion-factors).  

`R` code and data for the analyses described here are available on GitHub at https://github.com/salmonwatersheds/state-of-salmon.

## Region-Specific Data Sources

Here we describe specific data sources for the abundance of salmon and steelhead at the regional scale. 

```{r load data dependencies, echo=FALSE}

regions <- c("Yukon", "Transboundary", "Haida Gwaii", "Nass", "Skeena", "Central Coast", "East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets", "West Vancouver Island", "Fraser", "Columbia")

species_vec <- c("Chinook", "Chum", "Coho", "Pink", "Sockeye", "Steelhead")

# Generation length by species and region (for smoothing)
genLength <- read.csv(here("data/gen_length_regions.csv"))

# Set version of NuSEDS for source_id
nuseds_id <- "PSF_20260428"
ctc_id <- "CTC_20260818"

# Initiate dataframe
sps_data <- NULL

# Dropbox location for archiving
Dropbox_dir <- paste0(get_XDrive(), "1_PROJECTS/1_Active/State of Salmon/2_Data & Analysis/state-of-salmon")
```

### Yukon
The Canadian portion of the Yukon River is home to Chinook, chum, and coho salmon. Border escapement and total abundance (i.e. run size) of Canadian-origin Chinook and fall chum salmon in the mainstem Yukon River are counted at the Eagle Sonar station on the Yukon/Alaska border, and are available from the [Yukon River Panel](https://www.yukonriverpanel.com/) in their Joint Technical Committee (JTC) Reports. 

There are also Chinook, chum, and coho salmon in the Canadian portion of the Porcupine River, which joins the mainstem Yukon River in Alaska. Data on escapement to the Porcupine River are more patchy and not currently included here.


#### Chinook {.unnumbered}
We used Chinook `RR Spawning escapement estimate` and `RR Canadian origin total run size estimate` from Appendix B11 of @YukonRiverJointTechnicalCommittee2025YukonRiverSalmon. 

<!-- There is no coho compiled here - why listed above? -->

```{r yukon chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Yukon River Chinook salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}

# Load data ---
ytck <- read.csv(here('data/yukon_chinook_appendixB11.csv'), na.strings = "-") 
# Note: Use Run Reconstruction (RR) estimates of spawning escapement and total
# run size, not "Historical" or Mark-Recapture estimates

# Check if years are continuous
#unique(diff(ytck$Year)) # Yes, all one year apart # commented out to avoid outputting in Rmd

# Reformat data for SPS ---
ytck_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Yukon", dim(ytck)[1]),
	species = rep("Chinook", dim(ytck)[1]),
	year = ytck$Year,
	spawners = ytck$RR.Spawning.escapement.estimate, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = ytck$RR.Canadian.origin.total.run.size.estimate,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep("JTC_202603", dim(ytck)[1])
) 

# Smoothing
ytck_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = ytck_sps$spawners,
	years = ytck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Yukon" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
	)

ytck_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = ytck_sps$runsize,
	years = ytck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Yukon" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

# Add to SPS data
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, ytck_sps)

# Generate standard plot
plot_abund(ytck_sps)

```

#### Chum {.unnumbered}

Canadian-origin fall chum spawner abundance was taken as the `Spawning escapement estimate` in Appendix B16 and total abundance as the `Total estimated Canadian-origin run size` from Appendix B20 of @YukonRiverJointTechnicalCommittee2025YukonRiverSalmon. 

```{r yukon chum, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Yukon River chum salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each. We use the spawning escapement from Appendix B16 for spawner abundance, while the escapement data from Appendix B20 makes up part of the total abundance. There are small differences between the two datasets in the early 2000s."}
# Load data ---
ytcm_B16 <- read.csv(here('data/yukon_chum_appendixB16.csv')) # Historical data
names(ytcm_B16)[1] <- "Year"
ytcm_B20 <- read.csv(here('data/yukon_chum_appendixB20.csv')) # Most recent estimates

# Check if years are continuous
#unique(diff(ytcm_B16$Year)) # Yes, all one year apart
#unique(diff(ytcm_B20$Year)) # Yes, all one year apart

# Reformat data for SPS
ytcm_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Yukon", dim(ytcm_B16)[1]),
	species = rep("Chum", dim(ytcm_B16)[1]),
	year = ytcm_B16$Year,
	spawners = ytcm_B16$Spawning.escapement.estimate, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = ytcm_B20$Total.estimated.Canadian.origin.run.size[match(ytcm_B16$Year, ytcm_B20$Year)],
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep("JTC_202603", dim(ytcm_B16)[1])
) 

# Smoothing
ytcm_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = ytcm_sps$spawners,
	years = ytcm_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Yukon" & genLength$species == "Chum"]
)

ytcm_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = ytcm_sps$runsize,
	years = ytcm_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Yukon" & genLength$species == "Chum"]
)

# Add to SPS data
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, ytcm_sps)

# Generate standard plot
plot_abund(ytcm_sps, cols = c("#000000", grey(0.6), 2), red_points = "Spawner (Appendix B20)")
points(ytcm_B20$Year, ytcm_B20$Spawning.escapement*10^-3, col = 2, pch = 19, cex = 0.6)



```


### Northern Transboundary
<!-- > Internal note: Processing of raw excel file from Aaron Foos to extract relevant tables and fields is in code/tbr-data-extract.R -->

The best-available information on salmon abundance in the Northern Transboundary region is from the PSC's [Joint Transboundary Technical Committee Reports](https://www.psc.org/publications/technical-reports/technical-committee-reports/transboundary/). The most recent TTC report [@TTC2025FinalEstimatesTransboundary] includes data through 2023. Updated report appendices were provided by Aaron Foos (DFO) on July 8, 2026 in advance of report publication, and numbers for 2024-2025 should be considered **preliminary**.

We recognize that our approach in the Transboundary lacks information from many un-monitored watersheds, in particular the smaller watersheds of the Chilkat, Unuk, and Whiting Rivers. In the absence of better monitoring, we choose to report available data as a proxy for regional abundance, and note that the contribution of these smaller watersheds to total regional abundance for each species is likely small. 


#### Chinook {.unnumbered}
The regional spawner abundance and total return of Chinook was calculated as the sum of escapement and total return, respectively, to the Stikine, Alsek, and Taku indicator stocks. For each of these stocks, we used escapement and exploitation rates provided by the [PSC's Chinook Technical Committee](https://www.psc.org/publications/technical-reports/technical-committee-reports/chinook/) as part of their Synoptic Evaluations of Stock Status. These data were downloaded from their [Data Application](https://psc1.shinyapps.io/ctc-shiny-app/_w_efbbad27/). Total abundance was calculated from the escapement, $E$, and exploitation rate, $r$, as $E/(1-r)$. 


For 2025, the Synoptic Evaluations of Stock Status are not yet available. We used the escapement estimates for Stikine, Alsek, and Taku Chinook from Table B2 of Appendix B - Detailed Escapement, available as a downloadable dataset from the [Chinook Technical Committee](https://www.psc.org/publications/technical-reports/technical-committee-reports/chinook/ctc-data-sets/). Canadian and US harvest of Chinook provided by Aaron Foos (DFO) as updated tables from the Transboundary Technical Committee report. Specifically, harvest for Stikine Chinook from Table B12 and harvest of Taku Chinook from Table D8. Total harvest of Alsek Chinook was provided by Teresa Wallace (DFO, pers. comm.): US Commercial: 194, US Subsistence: 8, CAN (Aboriginal): 94, CAN Recreational: 0 (No CAN recreational harvest permitted in 2025) (Total harvest = 296).

```{r transboundary chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Transboundary chinook salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}
# Load data ---

# Get Synoptic evaluation data (up to 2024)
tbrck_raw <- read.csv(here("data/CTC_Synoptic_evaluation_data_all_2026-08-19.csv")) %>%
	filter(Year > 1975) %>% # Remove 1975 -> missing Alsek data
	filter(Stock %in% c("Alsek", "Taku", "Stikine")) %>%
	dplyr::select(Stock, Year, Escapement, RateType, Rate) %>%
	mutate(TotalRun = Escapement/(1 - Rate))

# Get CTC detailed escapement (Appendix B) data - for 2025
tbrck_esc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B2", range = "A5:G54", col_names = c("year", "Alsek_esc", "Alsek_cv", "Taku_esc", "Taku_cv", "Stikine_esc", "Stikine_cv")) %>%
	mutate(Total_esc = Alsek_esc + Taku_esc + Stikine_esc)

# 2025 Harvest data - from data provided by Aaron Foos on 2026-07-08 and Teresa Wallace on 2026-08-21
tbrck_harvest <- data.frame(Year = rep(c(2025), 3), 
													 Stock = rep(c("Alsek", "Taku", "Stikine")),
													 CAD_harv = c(94, 44, 263),
													 USA_harv = c((194+8), 857, 12)) %>%
								mutate(Total_harv = CAD_harv + USA_harv)

# For 2025, take harvest from TTC B12, D8, Provided by Aaron Foos; Alsek harvest provided by email (Teresa Wallace, DFO)
tbrck <- tbrck_raw %>%
	group_by(Year) %>%
	summarise(Escapement_all = sum(Escapement),
						TotalRun_all = sum(TotalRun), 
						source_id = "PSC_20260819") %>%
	bind_rows(data.frame(Year = 2025,
						Escapement_all = (tbrck_esc$Alsek_esc + tbrck_esc$Taku_esc + tbrck_esc$Stikine_esc)[tbrck_esc$year == 2025],
						TotalRun_all = sum(tbrck_harvest$Total_harv) + tbrck_esc$Total_esc[tbrck_esc$year == 2025], # Total run = sum of escapements and harvests
						source_id = "Foos_20260708"))


# Reformat data for SPS
tbrck_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Northern Transboundary", length(tbrck$Year)),
	species = rep("Chinook", length(tbrck$Year)),
	year = tbrck$Year,
	spawners = tbrck$Escapement_all, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = tbrck$TotalRun_all,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = tbrck$source_id
) 

# Smoothing
tbrck_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = tbrck_sps$spawners,
	years = tbrck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Northern Transboundary" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

tbrck_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = tbrck_sps$runsize,
	years = tbrck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Northern Transboundary" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

# Plot abund using ggplot instead of base?

# plot_abund(tbrck_sps)

ggplot(tbrck_sps, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = spawners/1000, colour = "Spawner"), lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = spawners/1000, colour = "Spawner"), 
             pch = 21, fill = "white") +
  geom_line(aes(y = runsize/1000, colour = "Total"), lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = runsize/1000, colour = "Total"), 
             pch = 21, fill = "white") +
  geom_line(aes(y = smoothedRunsize/1000), lwd = 1.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = smoothedSpawners/1000), 
            lwd = 1.2, colour = grey(0.6)) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Spawner" = grey(0.7),
      "Total" = "black"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Northern Transboundary Chinook",
    y = "Abundance (thousands)"
  ) +
  lims(
    y = c(0, max(c(tbrck_sps$spawners, tbrck_sps$runsize), 
                 na.rm = TRUE)/1000)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.98, 0.98),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top")
  )

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, tbrck_sps)

```

```{r transboundary chinook figs, echo = FALSE, include = TRUE, results = 'asis', fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "**Above:**  Northern Transboundary Chinook salmon (a) spawner abundance and (b) total abundance showing the contributions of the Alsek, Taku, and Stikine river basins."}

# Update 2025 data by system - from Appendix B detailed escapement data
tbrck_raw_updated <- tbrck_raw %>%
	rbind(data.frame( # 2025 data  (From data provided by Aaron Foos)
		Stock = c("Taku", "Stikine", "Alsek"),
		Year = rep(2025, 3),
		Escapement = c(tbrck_esc$Taku_esc[tbrck_esc$year==2025], 
									 tbrck_esc$Stikine_esc[tbrck_esc$year==2025],
									 tbrck_esc$Alsek_esc[tbrck_esc$year==2025]), 
		RateType = rep(NA, 3),
		Rate = rep(NA, 3),
		TotalRun = rep(NA, 3)))

# For 2025, take harvest from TTC B12, D8, Provided by Aaron Foos; Alsek harvest provided by email (Teresa Wallace, DFO)
tbrck_harvest <- data.frame(Year = rep(c(2025), 3), 
													 Stock = rep(c("Alsek", "Taku", "Stikine")),
													 CAD_harv = c(94, 44, 263),
													 USA_harv = c((194+8), 857, 12)) %>%
								mutate(Total_harv = CAD_harv + USA_harv)

# Calculate Total Run for 2024 and 2025
tbrck_raw_updated_25 <- tbrck_raw_updated %>% 
	filter(Year == 2025) %>%
	left_join(tbrck_harvest, by=c("Year", "Stock")) %>%
	mutate(TotalRun = Escapement + Total_harv)
	
tbrck_raw_updated$TotalRun[tbrck_raw_updated$Year == 2025] <- tbrck_raw_updated_25$TotalRun

# Plot ---

# Spawner abundance
spwn.stack <- tbrck_raw_updated %>% ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=Year, y=Escapement/1000, fill=factor(Stock, levels=c("Alsek", "Taku", "Stikine"))), 
								alpha=0.6) + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Spawner abundance (thousands)", fill="") + lims(y=c(0,185)) +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")

# Total abundance
tot.stack <- tbrck_raw_updated %>% ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=Year, y=TotalRun/1000, fill=factor(Stock, levels=c("Alsek", "Taku", "Stikine"))), 
								alpha=0.6) + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Total abundance (thousands)", fill="") + lims(y=c(0,185)) +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")

cowplot::plot_grid(spwn.stack, tot.stack, labels="auto", nrow = 2, ncol = 1)

```

#### Sockeye {.unnumbered}

Sockeye spawner abundance and total return were taken from the updated TTC report appendices. Specifically, Stikine sockeye spawner and total abundance were the `Escapement/broodstock` and `Terminal Run`, respectively, summed across the Stikine River (Appendix B26) and the Taku River (Appendix D17). 

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = TRUE, results = 'asis', fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "**Above:** Sockeye salmon spawner abundance (top) and total abundance (bottom) in the Taku and Stikine river basins. We report regional abundance only from 1984 onwards when data for both rivers are available; prior to 1984, only dat for the Stikine are available."}

# TBR Sockeye data are the sum of the Stikine (Appendix B26) and Taku (Appendix D17) 
# In 2024, the Appendix numbers given were B21 and D15 respectively, but that's changed.
tbrse_stik <- read.csv(here('data/tbr_sockeye_appendixB26.csv'))
tbrse_taku <- read.csv(here('data/tbr_sockeye_appendixD17.csv'))

# Combine
tbrse_raw <- tbrse_stik %>%
	rename("Escapement" = "StikineRiver_EscapementBroodstock",
				 "TotalRun" = "StikineRiver_TerminalRun") %>%
	mutate(Stock = "Stikine") %>%
	bind_rows(tbrse_taku %>%
							rename("Escapement" = "Escapement",
										 "TotalRun" = "Run") %>%
							mutate(Stock = "Taku")	)
# Plot ---

# Spawner abundance
spwn.stack <- tbrse_raw %>% ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=Year, y=Escapement/1000, fill=factor(Stock, levels=c("Taku", "Stikine"))), 
								alpha=0.6) + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Spawner abundance (thousands)", fill="") + #lims(y=c(0,185)) +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")

# Total abundance
tot.stack <- tbrse_raw %>% ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=Year, y=TotalRun/1000, fill=factor(Stock, levels=c( "Taku", "Stikine"))), 
								alpha=0.6) + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Total abundance (thousands)", fill="") + #lims(y=c(0,185)) +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")

cowplot::plot_grid(spwn.stack, tot.stack, labels="auto", nrow = 2, ncol = 1)

```


```{r transboundary sockeye, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Transboundary sockeye salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}

# Remove Stikine data prior to 1984
tbrse_stik <- subset(tbrse_stik, tbrse_stik$Year >= 1984)

# Reformat data for SPS
tbrse_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Northern Transboundary", dim(tbrse_stik)[1]),
	species = rep("Sockeye", dim(tbrse_stik)[1]),
	year = tbrse_stik$Year,
	spawners = tbrse_stik$StikineRiver_EscapementBroodstock + tbrse_taku$Escapement, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = tbrse_stik$StikineRiver_TerminalRun + tbrse_taku$Run,
	smoothedRunsize = NA, 
	source_id = rep("Foos_20250415", dim(tbrse_stik)[1])
) 

# Smoothing
tbrse_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = tbrse_sps$spawners,
	years = tbrse_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Northern Transboundary" & genLength$species == "Sockeye"]
)

tbrse_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(

#### Chum, pink, and steelhead {.unnumbered}

Monitoring of chum salmon, pink salmon, and steelhead in the Transboundary region is limited, and the best available information is the Canyon Island fish wheel on the Taku River. Data from the fish wheel are reported in the annual Transboundary Technical Committee reports. The window of operation, number of operating days, and hours of operation have varied from year to year, and thus the raw counts are not a reliable index of abundance through time. For example, fish wheel operation decreased from 24 hours to 16 hours per day in 2018 and further to 8 hours a day in 2023 [@TTC2025FinalEstimatesTransboundary]. 

```{r canyon-island-fw, fig.cap="**Above:**  Operation of the Canyon Island fish wheel on th Taku River from 1982 to 2025: a) Operating window each year occurred between April and October. (b) Total number of operating days varied between 73 and 172 with an average of 138.8, while the hours of operation each day decreased from 24 (1982-2017) to 16 (2018-2022) to 8 (2023-2025).", fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}

appD24 <- read_xlsx(here("data/2025 PSF Pacific Salmon Explorer Data.xlsx"), sheet = "TAK Appen D.24", range = "A8:P50")

# Calculate annual operating days
z <- strsplit(appD24$Operation, split = "-")
operationDates <- data.frame(
	Year = appD24$Year,
	startDate = NA,
	endDate = NA
)
ny <- length(appD24$Year)

for(i in 1:ny){
	operationDates$startDate[i] <- as.Date(paste0(z[[i]][1], "/", operationDates$Year[i]), format = "%m/%d/%Y")
	operationDates$endDate[i] <- as.Date(paste0(z[[i]][2], "/", operationDates$Year[i]), format = "%m/%d/%Y")
}

operationDates$nDays <- operationDates$endDate - operationDates$startDate + 1
operationDates$startDate <- as.Date(operationDates$startDate, origin = "1970-01-01")
operationDates$endDate <- as.Date(operationDates$endDate, origin = "1970-01-01")

operationDates$startMonth <- as.numeric(strftime(operationDates$startDate, format = "%m"))
operationDates$startDay <- as.numeric(strftime(operationDates$startDate, format = "%d"))
operationDates$endMonth <- as.numeric(strftime(operationDates$endDate, format = "%m"))
operationDates$endDay <- as.numeric(strftime(operationDates$endDate, format = "%d"))

par(mfrow = c(2,1), mar = c(3,4,1,4), oma = c(0,0,2,0), family = "Arial")
plot(range(operationDates$Year), as.Date(c("2000-04-01", "2000-10-31")), "n", xlab= "", ylab = "Operating window", las = 1, bty = "l")
abline(h = as.Date(paste(rep(2000, 8), c(4:11), rep(1, 8), sep = "-")), lty = 2)
for(i in 1:ny){
	segments(x0 = operationDates$Year[i],
					 x1 = operationDates$Year[i],
					 y0 = as.Date(paste(2000, operationDates$startMonth[i], operationDates$startDay[i], sep = "-")),
					 y1 = as.Date(paste(2000, operationDates$endMonth[i], operationDates$endDay[i], sep = "-")),
					 lwd = 5, lend = 1)
}
mtext(side = 3, line = 0.5, adj = 0, "a)")

plot(operationDates$Year, operationDates$nDays, "o", pch = 21, bg = 'white', ylab = "Number of operating days", xlab = "", las = 1, bty = "l")		
par(new = TRUE)
plot(appD24$Year, appD24$hours, "l", col = 2, xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", lwd = 2)
axis(side = 4, col = 2, las = 1)
mtext(side = 3, line = 0.5, adj = 0, "b)")

mtext(side = 3, outer= TRUE, "Canyon Island Fish Wheel Operation")
mtext(side = 4, "Operating hours per day", col = 2, line = 2.5)

```

To account for changes in fish wheel operation through time we calculate an index of abundance for chum, pink, and steelhead as the annual catch per unit effort (CPUE) multiplied by the average effort across all years. Catch per unit effort (CPUE) is calculated each year as the raw count $C_t$ divided by the operating days:
$$ \text{CPUE }_t = \frac{C_{t}}{d_t \times h_t/24} $$
where $d_t$ is the number of operating days in year $t$ and $h_t$ is the operating hours per day. The resulting index of abundance was used as the spawner abundance for the regional population.

```{r transboundary-cpue, echo = FALSE}

avgDays <- mean(operationDates$nDays * appD24$hours/24)

# Merge datasets
tbr_cmpksh <- appD24 %>% left_join(operationDates) %>%
	dplyr::select(Year, Operation, startDate, endDate, nDays, hours, Pink_12, Chum, Steelhead_3) %>%
	rename("pink_raw" = "Pink_12",
				 "chum_raw" = "Chum",
				 "steelhead_raw" = "Steelhead_3") %>%
	# Calculate CPUE, where effort is fish wheel days
	mutate(pink_cpue = pink_raw/(nDays * hours/24),
				 chum_cpue = chum_raw/(nDays * hours/24),
				 steelhead_cpue = steelhead_raw/(nDays * hours/24)) %>%
	# calculate adjusted (standardized) index based on average number of days
	mutate(pink_adj = pink_cpue * avgDays,
				 chum_adj = chum_cpue * avgDays,
				 steelhead_adj = steelhead_cpue * avgDays)
				 
```

##### Steelhead {.unnumbered}

Steelhead trout have also been enumerated at the Canyon Island fish wheel since 1987, though in past versions of datasets estimates have been patchy and the timing of the fish wheel likely misses a substantial portion of the Taku summer run steelhead. Thus, we have not previously used the Canyon Island counts. However, the 2026 dataset included a more complete time series for Steelhead and we were able to adjust for changes in fish wheel operation as described above. 

```{r transboundary steelhead, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance of Transboundary steelhead. The raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average. Red points show the raw fish wheel counts, which were used to calculate an index of abundance based on CPUE."}


# Reformat data for SPS
tbrsh_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Northern Transboundary", nrow(tbr_cmpksh)), 
	species = rep("Steelhead", nrow(tbr_cmpksh)), 
	year = tbr_cmpksh$Year, 
	spawners = tbr_cmpksh$steelhead_adj, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = NA,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep("Foos_20260708", nrow(tbr_cmpksh))
) %>% filter(year > 1986) # Take out early years with no steelhead data

# Smoothing
tbrsh_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = tbrsh_sps$spawners,
	years = tbrsh_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Northern Transboundary" & genLength$species == "Steelhead"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, tbrsh_sps)

# Generate standard plot
plot_abund(tbrsh_sps, red_points = "Raw fish wheel count")
points(tbr_cmpksh$Year, tbr_cmpksh$steelhead_raw*10^-3, col = 2, pch = 19, cex = 0.6)

```

### Haida Gwaii

#### Chinook {.unnumbered}
The only available data for Chinook salmon in Haida Gwaii are from a single enumeration project on the Yakoun River. Monitoring on the Yakoun has recently been restored. **More information about methods**

These estimates (prior to 2006) also match the estimated escapement to Area 1 in the  @NorthernBoundaryTechnicalCommittee2023USCanadaNorthern (Appendix 30).

```{r haida gwaii chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance of Haida Gwaii chinook salmon. The raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average. here, purple points are from NuSEDS spawner surveys and grey are from recent enumeration project."}

# Get spawner survey data to compare
hgck_ss <- read.csv(here("data/spawner_surveys.csv")) %>%
	subset(species_name == "Chinook" & region == "Haida Gwaii") %>%
	subset(stream_name_pse == "YAKOUN RIVER")

hgck <- read.csv(here("data/Yakoun_Chinook_1952-2025.csv"))

# There are some missing years of data; want to impute in between when smoothing
#diff(hgck$year)
hgck_years <- min(hgck$year):max(hgck$year)

# Reformat data for SPS
hgck_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Haida Gwaii", length(hgck_years)),
	species = rep("Chinook", length(hgck_years)),
	year = hgck_years,
	spawners = hgck$stream_observed_count[match(hgck_years, hgck$year)], 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = NA,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = c(rep(hgck$source_id[1], length(hgck_years[1]:2020)), 
								rep(hgck$source_id[nrow(hgck)], length(2021:2025)))
) 



# Smoothing
hgck_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = hgck_sps$spawners,
	years = hgck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Haida Gwaii" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, hgck_sps)

# Generate standard plot
plot_abund(hgck_sps)
points(hgck_ss$year, hgck_ss$stream_observed_count/1000, col="purple")

```

#### Chum {.unnumbered}
For chum, coho, pink, and sockeye in Haida Gwaii, we followed the [Expansion Factors](#expansion-factors) approach described below. We compared our expansion approach to estimates of Area 1 escapement as reported in the @NorthernBoundaryTechnicalCommittee2023USCanadaNorthern (Appendix 30), but found the Area 1 estimates were much lower for chum (see "alternate" series in figure below).

names(hg_table30) <- c("year", "Sockeye", "Coho", "Pink", "Chum", "Chinook") # Change names to be consistent with species

)

# Expansion plot(s)
plot_expansions(speciesname = "Sockeye",
								regionname = "Haida Gwaii",
								region_spawners = region_spawners,
								expansion_factors = expansion_factors,
								added_series = added_series.s)

```


### Nass

#### Chinook {.unnumbered}

**updated 2026**
We have estimates of escapement (spawners) and total run to 2025 from the [2025 Nass River Salmon Stock Assessment Post-Season Summary](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/ogfqvqj7u6uc95j17x4aw/2025-NFWD-Nass-Stock-Assessment-Update_Post-Season-v1-_2Dec25.pdf?rlkey=nwmx4hw42ts1tvxdi2prowm3m&dl=0), Tables 20 and 22. The escapement estimates correspond closely to those from the [PSC's Chinook Technical Committee (CTC) data sets](https://www.psc.org/publications/technical-reports/technical-committee-reports/chinook/ctc-data-sets/), though less so in 2018 and 2022 (purple open circles). The 'Total run' from the Nisgaa dataset is consistently higher than 't.run' from the CTC dataset (blue open circles), except in 2021 and 2022. **It is unclear whether one or both include marine fisheries?** Specifically, we use Nass River (Area 3) escapement and terminal run provided in Table B3 of the CTC report (fields `Esc` and `t.run` respectively).

```{r nass chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Nass chinook salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}
# Load data ---
# TCCHINOOK Table B3
nass_ctc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B3", range = "A5:D55", col_types = "numeric", col_names = c("Year", "Above_Gitwinksihlkw2", "Esc", "t.run"))

# Nisgaa data for comparison
nass_nisgaa <- read.csv(here("data/2025NassStockAssessment_Table20+22.csv"))

# Reformat data for SPS
nassck_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Nass", length(nass_ctc$Year)),
	species = rep("Chinook", length(nass_ctc$Year)),
	year = nass_ctc$Year,
	spawners = nass_ctc$Esc, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = nass_ctc$t.run,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep(ctc_id, length(nass_ctc$Year))
) 

# Smoothing
nassck_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = nassck_sps$spawners,
	years = nassck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Nass" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

nassck_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = nassck_sps$runsize,
	years = nassck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Nass" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, nassck_sps)

# Generate standard plot
plot_abund(nassck_sps)
points(x=nass_nisgaa$Year, y=nass_nisgaa$ESC_Chinook/1000, col="purple")
points(x=nass_nisgaa$Year, y=nass_nisgaa$TOTAL_RUN_Chinook/1000, col="blue") # Big difference! 

```



#### Sockeye {.unnumbered}

Nass sockeye escapement and total return were derived from the Northern Boundary Sockeye Run Reconstruction (NBSRR) Model that estimates total escapement and total return for the Skeena and Nass Rivers [@EnglishEtAl2017SkeenaSockeyeInriver; @EnglishEtAl2004AssessmentCanadianAlaskan]. Specifically, we used fields `TE` (Total Escapement) and `Total run` for Area 3 sockeye from the 2022 update to the North and Central Coast (NCC) Salmon Database Version 2, maintained by LGL Ltd. with support from PSF [@EnglishEtAl2018NorthCentralCoast; @ChallengerEtAl2018NorthCentralCoast]. For 2023-2025, we obtained the same model output from @NisgaaFisheriesandWildlifeDepartment20242024NassRiver. As can be seen in the figure below, historical numbers from these two sources closely matched, giving us confidence that it was justifiable to combine the two sources.

```{r nass sockeye, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Nass sockeye salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}

# Load Nisgaa data
nass_nisgaa <- read.csv(here("data/2025NassStockAssessment_Table20+22.csv"))

# use NBSRR data provided by LGL up to 2022 and Nisga'a Post-season for 2023, 2024
nassse <- read.csv(here("data/nassskeena_sockeye_lgl.csv")) %>%
	subset(Region == "Nass") %>%
	mutate(source_id = "English_20230930") %>%
	bind_rows(
		data.frame(Year = c(2023:2025),
							 TE = nass_nisgaa$ESC_Sockeye[nass_nisgaa$Year %in% c(2023:2025)],
							 Total.Run = nass_nisgaa$TOTAL_RUN_Sockeye[nass_nisgaa$Year %in% c(2023:2025)],
							 source_id = rep("Nisgaa_20251202", 3)
		)
	)


# Reformat data for SPS
nassse_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Nass", dim(nassse)[1]),
	species = rep("Sockeye", dim(nassse)[1]),
	year = nassse$Year,
	spawners = nassse$TE, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = nassse$Total.Run,
	smoothedRunsize = NA, 
	source_id = nassse$source_id
) 

# Smoothing
nassse_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = nassse_sps$spawners,
	years = nassse_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Nass" & genLength$species == "Sockeye"]
)

nassse_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = nassse_sps$runsize,
	years = nassse_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Nass" & genLength$species == "Sockeye"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, nassse_sps)

# Generate standard plot 
plot_abund(nassse_sps)

```

### Skeena

Chinook spawners were taken from the [PSC's Chinook Technical Committee (CTC) data sets](https://www.psc.org/publications/technical-reports/technical-committee-reports/chinook/ctc-data-sets/) and are reported on in @ChinookTechnicalCommittee2025AnnualReportCatch. Specifically, Skeena River (Area 4) escapement is provided in Table B3 (field `GSI esc`). There is no total return for the Skeena River provided in the CTC data sets.

**Purple open circles are escapement data from Table 32 of Joint Northern Boundary Technical Report [@JointNorthernBoundaryTechnicalCommittee2026USCanadaNorthern] for comparison.**

#### Sockeye {.unnumbered}
Skeena sockeye escapement and total return were derived from the Northern Boundary Sockeye Run Reconstruction (NBSRR) Model that estimates total escapement and total return for the Skeena and Nass Rivers [@EnglishEtAl2017SkeenaSockeyeInriver; @EnglishEtAl2004AssessmentCanadianAlaskan]. Specifically, we used fields `TE` (Total Escapement) and `Total run` for Area 4 sockeye from the 2022 update to the North and Central Coast (NCC) Salmon Database Version 2, maintained by LGL Ltd. with support from PSF [@EnglishEtAl2018NorthCentralCoast; @ChallengerEtAl2018NorthCentralCoast]. Data for 2023 were provided by Charmaine Carr-Harris (DFO) on request. **Data for 2024 are preliminary numbers from Joint Northern Boundary Technical Report [@JointNorthernBoundaryTechnicalCommittee2026USCanadaNorthern], but ideally we will receive data from Charmaine again. Purple open circles show Escapement estimates for 1970-2024 from Table 32 of the Joint Northern Boundary Technical Report.**

```{r skeena sockeye, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Skeena sockeye salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}

# Compare to NCC run reconstruction: https://github.com/LGLLimited/nccdbv2/tree/master/run/2022-nass-update/data/KarlEnglish-2023-05-29
skse_LGL <- read.csv(here("data/nassskeena_sockeye_lgl.csv")) %>%
	subset(Region == "Skeena") %>%
	mutate(source_id = "English_20230930")

# From PSC Run Size app:
skse_ch2 <- read.csv(here("data/Chapter2_Data_2025_07_22.csv")) %>%
	filter(Region == "Skeena River") %>%
	mutate(source_id = "PSC_20250722")

# Add 2023 data from Charmaine (pers. comm. July 24 2025)
skse_2023 <- data.frame(
	Year = 2023,
	TE = 1437788,
	catch = 656984
) %>%
	mutate(Total.Run = TE + catch,
	source_id = "CarrHarris_20250724")

# Add 2024 data from Joint Northern Boundary Tech Report
skse_2024 <- data.frame(
	Year = 2024,
	TE = 2683467,
	catch = NA
) %>%
	mutate(Total.Run = 2807467,
	source_id = NA)

# combine sources
skse <- skse_ch2[ , c("Year", "Spawners", "Returns", "source_id")] %>% # Use PSC data
	rename(TE = Spawners,
				 Total.Run  = Returns) %>%
	bind_rows(skse_LGL[which(skse_LGL$Year < 1982), c("Year", "TE", "Total.Run", "source_id")]) %>% # Use LGL data for pre-1982
	bind_rows(skse_2023[ c("Year", "TE", "Total.Run", "source_id")]) %>% # Add 2023 data from Charmaine
	bind_rows(skse_2024[ c("Year", "TE", "Total.Run", "source_id")]) %>% # Add 2024 data from NBTC report
	arrange(Year)


# Alternative source: NBTC report (all years included) for escapement
skse_nbtc <- read.csv(file=here("data/2026_Skeena_escapement_NBTC_Table32.csv"), na.strings = c("UNK", "UKN")) %>% select(YEAR, SOCKEYE)
	
#unique(diff(skse$Year)) # Yes, all one year apart

# Reformat data for SPS
skse_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Skeena", dim(skse)[1]),
	species = rep("Sockeye", dim(skse)[1]),
	year = skse$Year,
	spawners = skse$TE, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = skse$Total.Run,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = skse$source_id
) 

# Smoothing
skse_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = skse_sps$spawners,
	years = skse_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Skeena" & genLength$species == "Sockeye"]
)

skse_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = skse_sps$runsize,
	years = skse_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Skeena" & genLength$species == "Sockeye"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, skse_sps)

# Generate standard figure 
plot_abund(skse_sps)
points(x=skse_nbtc$YEAR, y=skse_nbtc$SOCKEYE/1000, col="purple")
```

### Central Coast

#### Chinook {.unnumbered}

For Central Coast Chinook, the PSC's Chinook Technical Committee (CTC) reported escapement for two indicator stocks on the Central Coast: the Atnarko River and Rivers Inlet [@ChinookTechnicalCommittee2025AnnualReportCatch]. Rivers Inlet is monitored "using an index of escapements to the Wannock, Kilbella, and Chuckwalla rivers" [@ChinookTechnicalCommittee2025AnnualReportCatch]. Because monitoring of Central Coast Chinook reported in NuSEDS has recently declined, expansions from spawner surveys are unreliable. As such, in 2025 we moved to using a composite indicator equal to the sum of the Atnarko River (`Total esc.`) and Rivers Inlet index reported by the CTC in Appendix Table B3.

```{r central coast chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance of Central Coast chinook salmon. The raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average."}

## Load data ---
# TCCHINOOK Table B3
cc_ctc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B3", range = "H5:K55", col_types = "numeric", col_names = c("Atnarko_Total_esc", "Atnarko_CV", "Atnarko_Wild", "Rivers_Inlet")) %>%
	mutate(Year = c(1975:2025))

# Reformat data for SPS
ccck_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Central Coast", length(cc_ctc$Year)),
	species = rep("Chinook", length(cc_ctc$Year)),
	year = cc_ctc$Year,
	spawners = cc_ctc$Atnarko_Total_esc + cc_ctc$Rivers_Inlet, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = NA,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep(ctc_id, length(cc_ctc$Year))
) 

# Smoothing
ccck_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = ccck_sps$spawners,
	years = ccck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Central Coast" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, ccck_sps)

#Generate standard figure
plot_abund(ccck_sps)

```


```{r central coast chinook figs, fig.cap = "**Above:**  Comparison of Chinook escapements on the Central Coast. The sum of Atnarko escapement (red) and Rivers Inlet escapement index (blue) from the CTC (purple points) was used in 2025. The expanded data from NuSEDS, not used, are in black with expansion factors used shown by grey 'x'"}
## Code to generate index comparison plot:
# Expanded spawner estimate
ccck_ex <- readRDS(here("output/expanded-spawners/Central Coast-spawners.rds"))[2, "Chinook", ]
yrs <- as.numeric(names(ccck_ex))

e <- readRDS(here("output/expanded-spawners/Central Coast-expansion-factors.rds"))[[1]]

# TCCHINOOK Table B3
cc_ctc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B3", 
														range = "H5:K55", col_types = "numeric", 
														col_names = c("Atnarko_Total_esc", "Atnarko_CV", 
																					"Atnarko_Wild", "Rivers_Inlet")) %>%
	mutate(Year = c(1975:2025))

par(mar = c(3,4,2,4))
plot(yrs, e$exp1, pch = 4, bty = "n", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", col = grey(0.6), ylim = c(0, 30), lwd = 2)
axis(side = 4, col = grey(0.6), las = 1)
mtext(side = 4, line = 2.5, "Expansion factor x", col = grey(0.6))
par(new = TRUE)

plot(yrs, ccck_ex*10^-3, "o", pch = 21, bg = "white", bty = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "Spawner abundance (thousands)", ylim = c(0, 150), las = 1, yaxs = "i")
abline(v = seq(1950, 2025, 5), lty = 3, col = grey(0.8))
abline(h = seq(0, 150, 50), lty = 3, col = grey(0.8))
points(cc_ctc$Year, cc_ctc$Atnarko_Total_esc*10^-3, "o", pch = 21, bg = "white", col = 2)
points(cc_ctc$Year, cc_ctc$Rivers_Inlet*10^-3, "o", pch = 21, bg = "white", col = 4)
points(cc_ctc$Year, cc_ctc$Atnarko_Total_esc*10^-3 + cc_ctc$Rivers_Inlet*10^-3, pch = 19, col = "purple", cex = 0.6)

legend("topleft", col = c(1,2,4, "purple"), c("NuSEDS expansion", "CTC Atnarko Total esc.", "CTC Rivers Inlet index esc.", "CTC sum"), pch = c(rep(21, 3), 19), pt.bg = "white", lwd = c(rep(1, 3),NA), bty = "n")

```



#### Steelhead {.unnumbered}

There are two spawner surveys for Steelhead trout on the Central Coast that we report in the Pacific Salmon Explorer. However, these surveys have been patchy through time with the most recent estimates from 2016. Therefore, spawner abundance and total return for Central Coast steelhead was considered unknown.


#### Chum {.unnumbered}

Estimates of spawner abundance for chum salmon on the Central Coast were expanded from available spawner surveys, as described below in [Expansion Factors](#expansion-factors). Monitoring and reporting of observed spawners on the Central Coast has declined in recent decades, thus requiring larger expansion factors to arrive at an area-wide estimate that can be compared through time. As such, estimates of spawner abundance for the Central Coast over the past decade are more uncertain and should be interpreted with caution. 

```{r central coast expansion data}
region_spawners <- sp <- readRDS(here("output/expanded-spawners/Central Coast-spawners.rds"))
yrs <- as.numeric(dimnames(sp)[[3]])
expansion_factors <- readRDS(here("output/expanded-spawners/Central Coast-expansion-factors.rds"))

```

	region = rep("Central Coast", length(cc.s)),
	species = rep("Chum", length(cc.s)),
	year = as.numeric(names(cc.s)),
	spawners = as.numeric(cc.s), 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = NA,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep(nuseds_id, length(cc.s)))

# Smoothing
cc.s_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = cc.s_sps$spawners,

	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Central Coast" & genLength$species == "Chum"])

# Add to master sps dataframe

# Generate standard figure

### East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets

In the 2025 State of Salmon report, we have split the former "Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets" region into two: East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets and West Vancouver Island. This split was made to better reflect the different ecology and habitats of salmon between the regions that may lead to different status and trends.

#### Chinook {.unnumbered}

PSC's Chinook Technical Committee (CTC) reports escapement (spawner abundance) and run size (total abundance) for three indicator stocks in the Strait of Georgia: Nanaimo, Cowichan, and Phillips [@ChinookTechnicalCommittee2025AnnualReportCatch]. We report spawner abundance and total abundance as the sum of `Esc` and `t.run`, respectively, across these three indicator stocks as reported in Appendix Table B4 available from the [PSC's Chinook Technical Committee (CTC) data sets](https://www.psc.org/publications/technical-reports/technical-committee-reports/chinook/ctc-data-sets/).

```{r east VI chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets chinook salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}
## Load data --
# (1) CTC data
evimi_ctc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B4", range = "A5:G55", col_types = "numeric", col_names = c("Year", "Nanaimo_esc", "Nanaimo_trun", "Cowichan_esc", "Cowichan_trun", "Phillips_esc", "Phillips_trun")) # Southern BC

evimi_ctc_summed <- evimi_ctc %>%
	group_by(Year) %>%
	summarise(esc_sum = sum(Nanaimo_esc, Cowichan_esc, Phillips_esc),
						trun_sum = sum(Nanaimo_trun, Cowichan_trun, Phillips_trun))

# Put in SPS format
evimick_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets", dim(evimi_ctc_summed)[1]),
	species = rep("Chinook", dim(evimi_ctc_summed)[1]),
	year = evimi_ctc_summed$Year,
	spawners = evimi_ctc_summed$esc_sum, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = evimi_ctc_summed$trun_sum,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep(ctc_id, dim(evimi_ctc_summed)[1])
) 

# Smoothing
evimick_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = evimick_sps$spawners,
	years = evimick_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

evimick_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = evimick_sps$runsize,
	years = evimick_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, evimick_sps)

#Generate standard figures
plot_abund(evimick_sps)
```


```{r east VI chinook figs, echo = FALSE, include = TRUE, results = 'asis', fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "**Above:**  (a) Chinook salmon spawner abundance and (b) total abundance showing the contributions of the Cowichan, Nanaimo, and Philips indicator stocks."}

evimi_ctc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B4", range = "A5:G55", col_types = "numeric", col_names = c("Year", "Nanaimo_esc", "Nanaimo_trun", "Cowichan_esc", "Cowichan_trun", "Phillips_esc", "Phillips_trun")) # Southern BC
	

# Spawner abundance
spwn.stack <- evimi_ctc %>% 
	tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -Year,
    names_to = c("stock", ".value"),  # .value keeps variable names (height, weight)
    names_sep = "_") %>%
	ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=Year, y=esc/1000, fill=stock), 
								alpha=0.6) + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Spawner abundance (thousands)", fill="") + lims(y=c(0,40)) +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")

# Total abundance
tot.stack <- evimi_ctc %>% 
	tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -Year,
    names_to = c("stock", ".value"),  # .value keeps variable names (height, weight)
    names_sep = "_") %>%
	ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=Year, y=trun/1000, fill=stock), 
								alpha=0.6) + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Spawner abundance (thousands)", fill="") + lims(y=c(0,40)) +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "right")

suppressWarnings(
cowplot::plot_grid(spwn.stack, tot.stack, rel_widths = c(0.75,1), labels="auto") )

```

```{r east VI expansion data}
region_spawners <- sp <- readRDS(here("output/expanded-spawners/East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets-spawners.rds"))

```{r east VI chum, results = 'asis', fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap="**Above:**  Spawner abundance of East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets chum salmon. The raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average."}

# Get rid of NAs (esp in 2024)

	spawners = as.numeric(evimi.s),

)

	abund = evimi.s_sps$spawners,
	years = evimi.s_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets" & genLength$species == "Chum"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe

```{r east VI chum figs, results = 'asis', fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "**Above:**  (a) Time series of spawner abundances showing raw sum of counts for indicator streams (red) and expanded estimates of spawner abudnance to indicator and non-indicator streams (black). This expanded time series is what is used to assess the current state and trends in spawner abundance for the region and species. (b) The values of Expansion Factor 1 that accounts for unmonitored indicator streams in a given year, and is calculated based on the proportional contribution of the unmonitored indicator stream(s) to the sum of all indicator streams in a (reference) decade."}

	filter(region == "East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets", species == "Chum") %>%

								regionname = "East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets",

	text(1953, 1.5, "Data prior to 1953 were discarded", adj = 0)
```

### West VI

In the 2026 State of Salmon report, we have split the former "Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets" region into two: East Vancouver Island & Mainland Inlets and West Vancouver Island. This split was made to better reflect the different ecology and habitats of salmon between the regions that may lead to different status and trends. 

#### Chinook {.unnumbered}
For Chinook spawner abundance, we used a 17-stream index of escapements from DFO (Nicholas Brown, pers. comm.). Streams were selected to represent WVI Chinook populations with minimal hatchery influence and infilling was done using data from neighbouring streams. For 2024 and 2025, this index was not yet available, but we reconstructed it using stream-level data from NuSEDS. We compare this below to the Chinook Technical Committee 14-stream index [@ChinookTechnicalCommittee2025AnnualReportCatch] used in the 2024 report (red circles) and find them similar [@ChinookTechnicalCommittee2025AnnualReportCatch].

Chinook total abundance was reported by DFO in 2025 [@DFO2025WestCoastVancouver]. The data shown in Figure 3 of @DFO2025WestCoastVancouver are available for download at https://zenodo.org/records/14847020 [accessed 25-Aug-2025]. We assumed that total abundance is the sum of the (non-terminal) ocean catch, hatchery-origin terminal return, and natural-origin terminal return. We note that this estimate of total abundance represents a total count of all Chinook from the region, and thus cannot be compared to the index of spawner abundance, which represents only a proportion of those fish. 

```{r west VI expansion data}

region_spawners <- sp <- readRDS(here("output/expanded-spawners/West Vancouver Island-spawners.rds"))
yrs <- as.numeric(dimnames(sp)[[3]])
expansion_factors <- readRDS(here("output/expanded-spawners/West Vancouver Island-expansion-factors.rds"))

```

```{r west VI chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of West Vancouver Island chinook salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}
## Load data ---
# 17 stream index from Nicholas Brown @ DFO (pers comm.)
wvi_ck <- read.csv(here("data/R-OUT_infilled_indicators_escapement_timeseries.csv")) %>% 
	group_by(year) %>% summarize(tot_esc = sum(escapement))
stream_lst <- read.csv(here("data/R-OUT_infilled_indicators_escapement_timeseries.csv")) %>% distinct(river)

# **Reconstructed** 17-stream index using NuSEDS data
nuseds_17 <- read.csv(here("data/spawner-survey-raw-wvi-ck.csv"))
nuseds_17_sum <- nuseds_17 %>% group_by(year) %>% 
	summarize(total_observed = sum(stream_observed_count)) %>%
	filter(year >=1979) # make it match the extent of the DFO data


# Compare the 17 stream index and our reconstructed version
wvi_ck %>% ggplot(aes(x=year, y=tot_esc/1000)) + geom_line(aes(col="DFO 17-Stream Index")) +
	geom_line(data=nuseds_17_sum, aes(x=year, y=total_observed/1000, col="Reconstructed 17-stream")) +
	scale_colour_manual(values = c("DFO 17-Stream Index" = "blue", "CTC 14-Stream Index" = "red", 
															 "Reconstructed 17-stream" = "purple")) +
	labs(col="Source", y="Spawner escapement (000s)", x="Year")


# Combine DFO 17-stream index from Nick brown with our reconstruction (2024,2025)
wvi_ck <- data.frame(year = c(wvi_ck$year, 2024:2025),
					 tot_esc = c(wvi_ck$tot_esc, 
					 						nuseds_17_sum$total_observed[nuseds_17_sum$year %in% 2024:2025]),
					 sourceid = c(rep("Brown_20260421", nrow(wvi_ck)), rep(nuseds_id, 2))
						)
wvi_ck <- wvi_ck %>% filter(year >=1985) # Total abundance only goes back to 1985, match that?

# Alternate (currently unused) source: 14 Stream index from CTC
wvi_ck_ctc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B5", range = "K24:K54", col_names = "WCVI_14Stream_Index") %>%
	mutate(Year = c(1995:2025)) # Escapement methods changed in 1995; only use earlier data for assessments

	
# Total abundance from Brown et al. 2025
wvi_ck_tot <- read_xlsx(here("data/WCVI_Chinook_total_abundance.xlsx"))
wvi_ck_tot$total_abundance <-  wvi_ck_tot$`Hatchery origin Terminal Return` + wvi_ck_tot$`Natural origin Terminal Return` +  wvi_ck_tot$`non-terminal Ocean catch`


# Put in SPS format
wvick_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("West Vancouver Island", nrow(wvi_ck)),
	species = rep("Chinook", nrow(wvi_ck)),
	year = wvi_ck$year,
	spawners = wvi_ck$tot_esc, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = c(wvi_ck_tot$total_abundance, NA, NA),
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = wvi_ck$sourceid # update source ID 
) 

# Smoothing
wvick_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = wvick_sps$spawners,
	years = wvick_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "West Vancouver Island" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)

wvick_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = wvick_sps$runsize,
	years = wvick_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "West Vancouver Island" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)


if(1 == 2){ # Visualize the time peries put on the same scale
	avg <- c(spawners = exp(mean(log(wvick_sps$spawners), na.rm = TRUE)),
	total = exp(mean(log(wvick_sps$runsize), na.rm = TRUE)))

	plot(wvick_sps$year, (wvick_sps$smoothedRunsize - avg[2])/avg[2], "o", pch = 19)
	abline(h= avg[2])
	points(wvick_sps$year, (wvick_sps$smoothedSpawners - avg[1])/avg[1], "o", col = grey(0.6))

}
# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, wvick_sps)

# Generate standard plot
plot_abund(wvick_sps)

# Generate plot of spawners ONLY so CTC comparison is more visible
wvi_ck %>% ggplot(aes(x=year, y=tot_esc/1000)) + 
geom_line(aes(col="DFO 17-Stream Index")) +
geom_point(aes(col="DFO 17-Stream Index"), shape=21) +
geom_point(data=wvi_ck_ctc, aes(x=Year, y=WCVI_14Stream_Index/1000, col="CTC 14-Stream Index"), shape=21) +
geom_line(data=wvi_ck_ctc, aes(x=Year, y=WCVI_14Stream_Index/1000, col="CTC 14-Stream Index"), alpha=0.5) +
scale_colour_manual(values = c("DFO 17-Stream Index" = "grey50", "CTC 14-Stream Index" = "red")) +
	labs(col="Source", y="Spawner escapement (000s)", x="Year") +
	theme_minimal() +
	theme(legend.position=c(0.6, 0.9))

```


#### Sockeye {.unnumbered}
Reconstructions of sockeye spawners and recruitment are compelted by DFO (Nicholas Brown, pers. comm.) for three Conservation Units on West Vancouver Island: Sproat, Great Central, and Hucuktlis (formerly Henderson). We used the sum of spawners and total return for these three Conservation Units as the index of sockeye spawner and total abundance for WVI. We acknowledge that this index does not account for lake-type sockeye in other watersheds (e.g., Muchalat, Kennedy, Clayoquot) or river-type sockeye in West Vancouver Island and Northwest Vancouver Island CUs, which tend to be in much lower abundance.

```{r west VI sockeye, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of West Vancouver Island sockeye salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}

# Sum of CU abundance from Sproat, Great Central, and Henderson
## Load data ---
wvi_se_raw <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/Barkley_Sockeye_stock-recruit_infilled.xlsx"), sheet = "S-R data")

wvi_se_summed <- wvi_se_raw %>%
	dplyr::select(year, stock, S, N) %>% # S = escapement, N = annual terminal run size
	filter(year >= 1977) %>% # Remove 1972 to 2076 for HUC because not available for other stocks
	group_by(year) %>%
	summarise(totalS = sum(S),
						totalN = sum(N))

# plot(wvi_se_summed$year, wvi_se_summed$totalN, "o", ylim = c(0, 2e6), main = "WVI Sockeye", xlab = "", ylab = "")
# points(wvi_se_summed$year, wvi_se_summed$totalS, "o",  col = 2)
# points(yrs, sp[2, "Sockeye", ], "o", col = 4)
# legend("topleft", col = c(1,2,4), c("3 CU - Total run", "3 CU - Escape.", "NuSEDS expanded"), pch = 1, lty = 1)

# Reformat data for SPS
wvise_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("West Vancouver Island", dim(wvi_se_summed)[1]),
	species = rep("Sockeye", dim(wvi_se_summed)[1]),
	year = wvi_se_summed$year,
	spawners = wvi_se_summed$totalS, 
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = wvi_se_summed$totalN,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep("Brown_20260420", dim(wvi_se_summed)[1])
) 

# Smoothing
wvise_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = wvise_sps$spawners,
	years = wvise_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "West Vancouver Island" & genLength$species == "Sockeye"]
)

wvise_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = wvise_sps$runsize,
	years = wvise_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "West Vancouver Island" & genLength$species == "Sockeye"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, wvise_sps)

# Generate standard figure
plot_abund(wvise_sps)

#### Pink {.unnumbered}

For West Vancouver Island pink salmon, spawner abundance was expanded from available spawner surveys, as described below in [Expansion Factors](#expansion-factors). The latest year of data (2025) were extracted from West Coast of Vancouver Island Stock Assessment bulletin dated November 15, 2024, and should be considered preliminary. We truncated the time series of spawner abundance to years 1953+ because earlier years had high expansion factor values indicating lack of monitoring on key indicator streams (see figures below). 

For chum, coho, and steelhead, we relied on NuSEDS' designations of indicator or non-indicator streams, but for pink salmon in this region we designated indicator streams as those with at least 10 years of data in the most recent 20 years. As a result, expansion factors were higher in historical years, but data from both indicator and non-indicator streams show markedly higher counts in the period 1960-1980 then in subsequent decades and it is unlikely that the observed decline is a result of uncertain expansions.

### Fraser

#### Chinook {.unnumbered}
<!-- River-level spawner abundance for Fraser Chinook found in NuSEDS can be highly unreliable, thus we based our expansions on only the most intensively monitored streams that have been deemed as reliable estimates of abundance by @BrownEtAl20202020SummaryAbundance. These streams are those shown in the [Pacific Salmon Explorer](https://www.salmonexplorer.ca), and the associated data can be accessed from the stream survey data in the [SWP Data Library](https://data.salmonwatersheds.ca/result?datasetid=1). We also truncated the Chinook index of abundance to 1984 and more recent data, as earlier years have been deemed unreliable [@BrownEtAl20202020SummaryAbundance] and from 1984 onward spawner estimates mirrored those reported by @AtlasEtAl2023TrendsChinookSalmon. For Chinook total return, we used the sum of total run for four Fraser populations (Harrison, Nicola, Lower Shuswap, and South Thompson - all) reported in @AtlasEtAl2023TrendsChinookSalmon and available from the associated [GitHub repository](https://github.com/willatlas/ChinookEscapement-RunSize). -->

Escapement and run size for Fraser Chinook were provided to PSF by Lauren Weir, DFO (pers. comm.). We took the sum of escapement and terminal run for five major stocks (Fraser Spring 4-2 (age 1.2), Fraser Spring 5-2 (age 1.3), Fraser Summer 5-2 (age 1.3), Fraser Summer 4-1 (age 0.3), and Harrison (Fraser Fall 4-1, age 0.3)). Escapement numbers match those in Table B6 of the [PSC's Chinook Technical Committee (CTC) data sets](https://www.psc.org/publications/technical-reports/technical-committee-reports/chinook/ctc-data-sets/) as shown by purple open circles below. The 't.run' in the CTC dataset excludes the Harrison stock.

```{r fraser chinook, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Fraser chinook salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}
# Data from Lauren Weir (shared 2026-04-24 by email)
frck <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/1975-2025 Fraser Chinook escapement and terminal run by SMU - for PSF.xlsx"), skip=1)
frck_smu <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/1975-2025 Fraser Chinook escapement and terminal run by SMU - for PSF.xlsx"), range="A1:K1", col_names=F) # get smu names
frck_smu <- rep(stringr::str_remove_all(frck_smu, "Fraser|age|-run|[[:punct:]]|[[:space:]]")[!is.na(frck_smu)], each=2)
names(frck)[2:ncol(frck)] <- paste(frck_smu, stringr::str_extract_all(names(frck)[2:ncol(frck)], "Esc|Run"), sep="_") # stitch together smu and col names
names(frck) <- stringr::str_to_lower(names(frck))


# Cut data to only 1984 onward when Harrison data were available.
frck <- frck %>% dplyr::filter(year >= 1984)

# Sum across SMUs
frck_esc <- round(apply(frck[, grep("esc", names(frck))], 1, sum))
frck_run <- round(apply(frck[, grep("run", names(frck))], 1, sum))

yrs <- frck$year

# Put in SPS format
frck_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Fraser", length(yrs)),
	species = rep("Chinook", length(yrs)),
	year = yrs,
	spawners = frck_esc,
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = frck_run,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = rep("Weir_20260424", length(yrs))
) 
	
	# Smoothing
frck_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
		abund = frck_sps$spawners,
		years = frck_sps$year,
		genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Fraser" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
	)

frck_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = frck_sps$runsize,
	years = frck_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Fraser" & genLength$species == "Chinook"]
)


# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, frck_sps)

# Generate standard figure
plot_abund(frck_sps)

# Load CTC data for comparison
frck_ctc <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/TCCHINOOK-2026-Appendix-B-Escapement-Detailed.xlsx"), sheet = "B6", range = "A5:G54", col_types = "numeric", col_names = c("Year", "Spr12_esc", "Spr13_esc", "Sum03_esc", "Sum13_esc", "SprSum_trun", "Harr_esc"))
frck_ctc <- frck_ctc %>% mutate(total_esc = Spr12_esc + Spr13_esc + Sum03_esc + Sum13_esc + Harr_esc)

# Plot comparison
points(x=frck_ctc$Year, y=frck_ctc$total_esc/1000, col="purple")

```


```{r fraser chinook figs, echo = FALSE, include = TRUE, results = 'asis', fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "**Above:**  (a) Aggregate escapement of Fraser Chinook with the contribution of escapement to each of five stocks shown as coloured regions. Note that the Harrison River (Fall 4-1) time series begins later (1984) than the other four stocks (1975), and thus we only report spawner abundance from 1984 onward. (b) The proportional contribution of each of five stocks to aggregate Fraser Chinook escapement."}
# Data from Lauren Weir (shared 2026-04-24 by email)
frck <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/1975-2025 Fraser Chinook escapement and terminal run by SMU - for PSF.xlsx"), skip=1)
frck_smu <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data/1975-2025 Fraser Chinook escapement and terminal run by SMU - for PSF.xlsx"), range="A1:K1", col_names=F) # get smu names
frck_smu <- rep(stringr::str_remove_all(frck_smu, "Fraser|age|-run|[[:punct:]]|[[:space:]]")[!is.na(frck_smu)], each=2)
names(frck)[2:ncol(frck)] <- paste(frck_smu, stringr::str_extract_all(names(frck)[2:ncol(frck)], "Esc|Run"), sep="_") # stitch together smu and col names
names(frck) <- stringr::str_to_lower(names(frck))


# Cut data to only 1984 onward when Harrison data were available.
frck <- frck %>% dplyr::filter(year >= 1984)

# Sum across SMUs
frck_esc <- round(apply(frck[, grep("esc", names(frck))], 1, sum))
frck_run <- round(apply(frck[, grep("run", names(frck))], 1, sum))

col_frck <- viridisLite::viridis(n = 5)

# Plot ---

# Spawner abundance
esc.stacked <- frck %>% 
	select(c(year, names(frck)[grepl(".esc$", names(frck))])) %>%
	rename('Spring 4-2' = 'spring12_esc',
				 'Spring 5-2' = 'spring13_esc',
				 'Summer 5-2' = 'summer13_esc',
				 'Summer 4-1' = 'summer03_esc', 
				 'Fall 4-1 (Harrison)' = 'harrisonfall03_esc') %>% 
	tidyr::pivot_longer(-1, names_to="Stock", values_to="Escapement") %>% 
	ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=year, y=Escapement/1000, fill=factor(Stock, levels=rev(unique(Stock)))), 
								alpha=0.6) + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Spawner abundance (thousands)", fill="") +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")




esc.sum <- frck %>% 
	select(c(year, names(frck)[grepl(".esc$", names(frck))])) %>%
	rename('Spring 4-2' = 'spring12_esc',
				 'Spring 5-2' = 'spring13_esc',
				 'Summer 5-2' = 'summer13_esc',
				 'Summer 4-1' = 'summer03_esc', 
				 'Fall 4-1 (Harrison)' = 'harrisonfall03_esc') %>% 
	tidyr::pivot_longer(-1, names_to="Stock", values_to="Escapement") %>% 
	filter(year >= 1984) %>% 
	ggplot() +
	geom_area(aes(x=year, y=Escapement/1000, fill=factor(Stock, levels=rev(unique(Stock)))), 
								alpha=0.6, position="fill") + 
	scale_fill_viridis_d() +
	labs(y="Proportion of spawner abundance (thousands)", fill="") +
	theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "right")

suppressWarnings(
cowplot::plot_grid(esc.stacked, esc.sum, labels="auto", rel_widths=c(0.75, 1))
)
```

#### Coho {.unnumbered}
**Updated 2026**
In 2026, Tanya Vivian (DFO) provided new IFC estimates dating back to 1984 (purple and blue circles). "Total Prefishery Abundance" is total return plus harvest, and can be considered equivalent to run size, while "Total Return" is spawners plus fish removed later for brood collection or AFC sacrifices (applicable only to the three indicator stocks). These respectively align exactly with our past data series until the 2010s when some small differences are introduced. For comparison, the old dataset is shown by purple and blue open circles for spawners and total abundance, respectively.


```{r fraser coho, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance (grey) and total abundance (black) of Fraser coho salmon. For both, the raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average for each."}
## Load data ---
frco <- readxl::read_excel(here("data/IFC-Data-TanyaVivian-2026.xlsx"), sheet=2) %>%
	summarize(Run.size = sum(Total.Prefishery.Abundance),
						Spawners = sum(Total.Return),
						Natural.Spawners = sum(Natural.Returns),
						Hatchery.Spawners = sum(`Hatchery Returns`), .by=ReturnYear)
frco_old <- read.csv(here("data/IFC_data_compiled.csv"))


# Put in SPS format
frco_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Fraser", length(frco$ReturnYear)),
	species = rep("Coho", length(frco$ReturnYear)),
	year = frco$ReturnYear,
	spawners = frco$Spawners, # Note this is the fish that returned to spawn, NOT a mistake!
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = frco$Run.size,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,
	source_id = "Vivian_20260527" # c(rep("Glavas_20231006", length(frco$year) - 2), rep("DFO_20250225", 2))
) 

# Smoothing
frco_sps$smoothedSpawners <- genSmooth(
	abund = frco_sps$spawners,
	years = frco_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Fraser" & genLength$species == "Coho"]
)

frco_sps$smoothedRunsize <- genSmooth(
	abund = frco_sps$runsize,
	years = frco_sps$year,
	genLength = genLength$gen_length[genLength$region == "Fraser" & genLength$species == "Coho"]
)

# Add to master sps dataframe
sps_data <- rbind(sps_data, frco_sps)

# Generate standard figure
plot_abund(frco_sps)
#points(frco_old$year, frco_old$spawners/1000, col="purple")
#points(frco_old$year, frco_old$runsize/1000, col="blue")

#### Steelhead {.unnumbered}
Steelhead trout in the Fraser are monitored by the Province in at least 10 different streams, but these data are not readily available. Relatively reliable estimates of steelhead spawner abundance are available at the CU-level for interior Fraser steelhead from the Thompson Summer CU (monitored at the Thompson River) and Mid Fraser Summer CU (primarily monitored at the Chilcotin River; data in the [Pacific Salmon Explorer](https://salmonexplorer.ca)). We used the sum of CU-level spawner abundance for these two CUs as an index of Fraser steelhead abundance. We note that this approach does not include more coastal populations, such as the Lower Fraser Summer steelhead monitored in the Coquihalla River or Boundary Bay Winter steelhead, which may not have declined to the same extent over the past decade. However, a lack of publicly accessible data on coastal Fraser steelhead has limited our ability to include these CUs in our index of abundance.

```{r fraser steelhead, fig.cap="**Above:** Spawner abundance of Fraser steelhead salmon. The raw data is shown by points and the smoothed metric by solid lines. Dashed horizonal lines represent the long-term average."}

	filter(region == "Fraser", species_name == "Steelhead") %>%
	filter(cu_name_pse %in% c("Thompson Summer", "Mid Fraser Summer")) %>%
	filter(!is.na(estimated_count) & estimated_count != -989898)

frsh_sum <- tapply(as.numeric(frsh$estimated_count), frsh$year, sum)
frsh_sum <- frsh_sum[min(which(!is.na(frsh_sum))): max(which(!is.na(frsh_sum)))]

# Put in SPS format
frsh_sps <- data.frame(
	region = rep("Fraser", length(frsh_sum)),
	species = rep("Steelhead", length(frsh_sum)),
	year = as.numeric(names(frsh_sum)),
	spawners = frsh_sum, # Note this is the fish that returned to spawn, NOT a mistake!
	smoothedSpawners = NA,
	runsize = NA,
	smoothedRunsize = NA,

) 

# Smoothing
